edits.headline: High-speed train crash in Spain kills at least 68 people
edits.subheadline: The train hit the rear of a stopped train near Urda, south of Madrid, CBS News and the Associated Press reported.
editorialBody: A high-speed train crashed into the rear of a stopped train near Urda, south of Madrid, killing at least 68 people, CBS News and the Associated Press reported. The Castilla-La Mancha regional government confirmed the death toll, CBS said. CNN and the Irish Times also reported at least 68 dead.

A police officer guarding the Israeli embassy in Belgrade shot dead an attacker carrying two knives just after midnight, the Associated Press reported. The officer was slightly wounded in the face, prosecutors said. Interior Minister Ivica Dacic said the attacker was a minor who supported the Islamic State group, and Serbia raised its terror threat level to the highest level, the AP said.

Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud was the largest party in Israel's election, with a projected 27 seats to 21 for Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party, the Jerusalem Post reported. Neither Netanyahu's bloc, with 53 seats, nor the opposition bloc, with 48, reached the 61 seats needed for a majority, Al Jazeera reported.

President Donald Trump said he would respect the results of the US midterm elections "if they're honest", the Korea Times reported. He made the remark as he left for a campaign trip to Texas, the paper said.
